children: Spain's competition watchdog has opened new sanction proceedings against Apple
, accusing the companies of failing to comply with an order to end anti-competitive practices involving the sale of Apple products on Amazon's Spanish website.

The  National Commission on Markets and Competition, or CNMC, said the companies did not remove the disputed contractual clauses until May 2025, despite being ordered to stop the practices in July 2023.

The regulator fined the companies a combined 194M euros ($224M) in 2023 for agreements that restricted the number of Apple product resellers on Amazon's Spanish website, limited advertising space for competing brands, and prevented Amazon from promoting rival products to Apple customers.
The CNMC said its council determined in October 2025 that the companies had failed to comply with the original order and directed its competition directorate to open new sanction proceedings.
The investigation could take up to three months. The regulator said opening the proceedings does not prejudge the outcome.
Both companies have appealed the original 2023 fine and the 2025 non-compliance decision to Spain's National Court, where the cases remain pending.

title: Spain's competition watchdog plans to sanction Apple, Amazon
